A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LOKI and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. The original case-study appendix is retained, moving from Appendix E in v1 to Appendix F in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original evaluations of language models, multimodal models, expert detectors and human participants across LOKI's five modalities.

after.justification: V2 retains those original evaluations and adds compression tests, deepfake-subset results, further prompting experiments and modality-specific difficulty analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, annotation and question-generation procedures, evaluation framework and existing prompting strategies are retained. The additional experiments do not introduce a new model or detection algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds JPEG-compressed images as an input-condition test scenario. The five modalities, underlying data sources and task types remain unchanged; the deepfake analysis explicitly evaluates components already present in LOKI.

E2.justification: V2 adds Random Choice and Human references to the image breakdown in Table 10 and a Human reference to the 3D breakdown in Table 13. Figure 5(c) replaces Idefics2-8B with Claude-3.5 in its displayed comparison. The principal evaluated model roster remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce five JPEG compression settings, from 100% to 60%, and CoT versus no-CoT comparisons for image multiple-choice and abnormal-selection tasks and video/text judgment. Existing main evaluation inputs, metrics and prompting procedures are retained; these additions do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix E substantially expands diagnostic analysis through compression robustness tests, deepfake-subset evaluation, prompting tests across additional task/modality combinations, and difficulty breakdowns by modality. V1 already contained aggregate difficulty, prompting, input-format and language/length analyses; its extensive case studies are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures. Point-estimate reporting and the existing human-evaluation repetition information remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 20–23 add substantial condition-specific results, alongside new reference entries in Tables 10 and 13. For example, Table 20 reports AIDE at 62.8% versus 45.2% under the 100% and 60% compression settings, while GPT-4o remains at 63.4% and 63.1%. Table 21 reports Claude-3.5-Sonnet at 0.14 on deepfakes versus 0.54 overall. Original main-table scores in Tables 2–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 retains the accuracy and Normalized Bias Index definitions and the GPT-based scoring scheme. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or mathematical derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, five-modality coverage, 26 categories and approximately 18K questions. Their central claims about detection capability, explainability, human-performance gaps and model limitations are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds substantive interpretations linking compression robustness to pretraining and model scale, deepfake failures to subtle forgery features, and prompting failures to context-handling limitations and possible interference from examples. It also reports incomplete or irrelevant LLaVA outputs as supporting observations. Section 4.3 removes 3D from its weak-modality statement, although the introduction retains that qualification.

D1.justification: V2 documents JPEG processing levels and participating models for the new compression experiment and revises the stated supported-model list in Appendix C.1. Existing model links, annotation instructions and dataset-request requirements remain essentially unchanged; the additions provide limited implementation detail.

R1.justification: V2 adds references concerning manipulation grounding, detector robustness, zero-shot CoT and voice synthesis/conversion, and removes the TinyLLaVA reference. These support the added discussion without substantially changing LOKI's positioning relative to existing benchmarks.

P1.justification: Changes include limited prose corrections, updated affiliations and conference headers, acknowledgments, and insertion of the new experimental appendix. The former case-study appendix becomes Appendix F and loses its modality subsection headings. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 20–23, inserts reference rows into Tables 10 and 13, and redraws Figure 5, including its radar traces, legend and text-task axis labels. Other illustrations and case-study figures are retained, with limited layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Appendix E provides useful evidence about compression robustness, deepfake failures and prompting dependence that strengthens the benchmark's diagnostic value beyond v1. The benefit is limited by reporting inconsistencies: the new human image-judgment result of 27.3 in Table 10 is unexplained relative to 80.1 in retained Table 2, and several new control scores lack sufficient setting details to reconcile them with earlier tables.
